sections.heading: Course creation for education and corporate learning
sections.body:
Educators and corporate learning teams need to turn subject matter into course content that can be reviewed and used. EduPilot supports rapid course creation for both settings.

Evaluate EduPilot using approved learning material to assess the course output against your objectives, audience and review requirements. Agree what your learning team needs to approve and how the content will move into your publishing workflow.

[Request an EduPilot demo](#get-in-touch) · [View all products](/products-and-accelerators)
sections.secondaryHeading: Keep course ownership with your learning team
sections.secondaryBody:
EduPilot is part of [Data & AI](/services/data-ai). [Agentic AI & GenAI](/services/data-ai/agentic-ai-genai) supports wider AI delivery, while [AI strategy & governance](/services/data-ai/ai-strategy-governance) helps define ownership, review and acceptable use.

The educator or subject-matter expert should approve content for factual accuracy, learning objectives and audience suitability before release.

sections.heading: Structure an authoring evaluation
sections.description: Assess EduPilot against your course requirements: suitable source material, draft structure and expert review. Confirm supported outputs and the hand-off to your publishing process.

items.title: Define the course
items.description: Set the audience, learning objectives and approved subject material. Establish how the material enters the authoring workflow and which source formats are supported.
items.bullets:
Input - course brief and approved material
Evaluation output - source and authoring scope

items.title: Develop a draft
items.description: Use the course-creation capability to assess an initial content draft. Check the organisation of the material and the extent to which it addresses the agreed objectives.
items.bullets:
Input - agreed learning objectives
Evaluation output - a course draft for expert review

items.title: Review before release
items.description: Have an educator or subject-matter expert assess the draft for accuracy and suitability. Confirm the supported hand-off and output formats; do not assume automatic LMS publication.
items.bullets:
Input - draft and review rubric
Evaluation output - approved content and a publishing plan

sections.heading: From course brief to reviewed content
sections.description: Evaluation workflow: establish the material, demonstrate course creation, review the draft and agree how approved content reaches your learning environment.

items.title: Set the brief
items.description: Choose a defined topic, audience and learning objectives. Use approved non-confidential material and identify its content owner.

items.title: Demonstrate authoring
items.description: Review a course draft produced in the demonstration. Establish source-material handling and the actual output structure.

items.title: Apply expert review
items.description: Check facts, relevance, tone and audience suitability. Record omissions or errors rather than treat generated material as ready to publish.

items.title: Agree the hand-off
items.description: Confirm content ownership, output formats and LMS or content integration needs. Assign the final release approval to the learning team.

sections.heading: Example: a corporate-learning module
sections.body:
**Example engagement pattern, not a client case study.** A corporate learning team wants to create a module from approved internal subject material. Define the audience and learning objectives, then evaluate a course draft against a subject-matter expert’s rubric.

The evaluation produces a course brief, sample draft, review and revision record, and a publishing plan. For an education evaluation, use the institution’s learning objectives and educator approval process to assess the draft’s suitability.

For broader operational workflow redesign, explore [Intelligent Operations](/solutions/intelligent-operations).

sections.heading: Agree your content and publishing boundaries
sections.description: Available by licence, subscription or SaaS, with or without Linkfields services. Request a course-creation demo using approved sample material, with an educator or learning lead involved.

items.title: What material and formats are supported?
items.description: Establish supported source types, authoring outputs and export formats in the demonstration. Confirm any LMS or content-system integration and the implementation work required. Course creation does not imply that EduPilot replaces an LMS or publishes automatically.

items.title: Who owns and approves the content?
items.description: Agree rights to source material and generated outputs, together with model-provider data use. Name the educator or subject-matter expert responsible for factual review, audience suitability and learning objectives. Confirm any grounding or review controls actually supported by the product.

items.title: What privacy and access controls apply?
items.description: Define content access, retention, tenant isolation and hosting/residency requirements. Do not provide confidential material or learner personal data for an initial demo. Any learner-facing use requires separate confirmation of privacy, age-appropriate safeguards and permitted scope.

items.title: What is included in the commercial scope?
items.description: Confirm available deployment options, licence or subscription terms and SaaS hosting scope. Separate product access from optional content integration, implementation, onboarding and managed support. Agree release and support responsibilities; product delivery does not guarantee learning outcomes.
